metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a grep command to the Testing section (or as an inline AC4 proving command) that asserts the absence of stale job names, e.g.: `grep -rn --include='*.md' --include='*.yaml' -E 'per-extra|union job|import-linter job' docs/ .github/ | grep -v 'docs/experiments/' && echo 'FAIL: stale references found' || echo 'OK'`
evidence: AC4: 'No reference to a per-extra, union, or import-linter JOB remains in docs/ or .github/, excluding docs/experiments/**'
Testing section only lists: 'make lint' and 'python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py' — neither scans for stale strings
findings.finding: AC4 asserts that no reference to 'per-extra', 'union', or 'import-linter' JOB remains in docs/ or .github/ (excluding docs/experiments/**), but the Testing section provides no grep/search command that would prove this negative-content claim. make lint and pytest do not detect stale job-name strings.
scenarios: An agent edits one file but misses the other; make lint and pytest still pass; AC4 is silently violated.
A future refactor reintroduces one of the old names in a doc comment; the absence assertion has no enforcement.
findings.suggested_fix:
Add to the Testing section:
```
# Prove AC4 — no stale job-name prose survives
grep -rn --include='*.md' --include='*.yaml' \
  -E '(per-extra|union job|import-linter[[:space:]]+job)' \
  docs/ .github/ \
  | grep -v 'docs/experiments/' \
  && { echo 'FAIL: stale references found'; exit 1; } \
  || echo 'OK: no stale references'
```
(Exit 1 on match makes this a proper gate.)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a brief audit step to the Approach (e.g., `grep -r 'per-extra\|import-linter' docs/ .github/ --include='*.md' --include='*.yaml' | grep -v docs/experiments`) confirming the two named files are the only occurrences, or tighten AC 4 to name only those two files if that is the intended scope.
evidence: AC 4: 'No reference to a `per-extra`, `union`, or `import-linter` JOB remains in `docs/` or `.github/`, excluding `docs/experiments/**` archival corpora.'
Scope: 'docs/llm-framework.md — the CI-enforcement clause … .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml — the `optionality` job's leading comment.'
Approach: 'Correct both passages' — only two passages are described, yet AC 4 covers an unbounded file set.
findings.finding: AC 4 asserts a sweeping negative — no stale `per-extra`, `union`, or `import-linter` JOB reference remains anywhere in `docs/` or `.github/` (except `docs/experiments/**`) — but the Scope and Approach describe editing exactly two files, with no search/audit step to verify no other occurrences exist. If a third location carries the stale wording, the AC fails without any plan guidance on how to find or fix it.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 4 vs. Scope section
scenarios: A third file in docs/ or .github/ carries the same stale wording; the implementer edits only the two scoped files, makes lint pass, but AC 4 still fails at review.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) add one sentence to Approach: 'A prior grep confirms these are the only two occurrences; no other files in `docs/` or `.github/` reference the removed job names.' — making the audit explicit and the AC verifiable; or (b) replace AC 4 with two file-specific lines matching the Scope.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either add `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` to scope (updating lines 3-5 to reflect the current job structure) or narrow AC4 to exclude historical-context commentary, so the AC is actually satisfiable by the stated edits.
evidence: AC4: 'No reference to a per-extra, union, or import-linter JOB remains in docs/ or .github/, excluding docs/experiments/** archival corpora.'
Scope: 'docs/llm-framework.md … .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml … Nothing else in either file changes.'
_optionality.yml line 3: '…the clean-core-wheel, per-extra, and union checks.'
_optionality.yml line 5: 'had a dedicated import-linter job here'
_optionality.yml line 114: 'what used to be a 5-cell per-extra matrix PLUS a separate union job'
ABSENCE: _optionality.yml is not listed as an edit target in Scope
findings.finding: AC4 requires that no reference to a per-extra, union, or import-linter JOB remains in docs/ or .github/ (excluding docs/experiments/**), but the plan's Scope only names two edit targets and explicitly states 'Nothing else in either file changes.' .github/workflows/_optionality.yml — which is not in scope — currently contains 'the clean-core-wheel, per-extra, and union checks' (line 3), 'had a dedicated import-linter job here' (line 5), and 'what used to be a 5-cell per-extra matrix PLUS a separate union job' (line 114). AC4 cannot pass with only the two stated edits.
scenarios: A reviewer or automated check runs AC4 verbatim against .github/workflows/_optionality.yml and finds per-extra/union/import-linter references, causing AC4 to fail even though both stated edits were made.
A future author reading _optionality.yml line 3 sees 'per-extra, and union checks' and is confused about whether those jobs still exist, perpetuating the exact rot the plan aims to fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Update _optionality.yml line 3 from 'the clean-core-wheel, per-extra, and union checks' to 'the clean-core-wheel and optional-extras checks' and revise the surrounding historical note at lines 4-5 to be consistent, then add _optionality.yml to the Scope section.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile scope and AC#4: either add `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` to the edit scope (updating its header comment and job `name:` to avoid the forbidden strings), or narrow AC#4 to explicitly exclude `_optionality.yml`'s self-description of its own per-extra-venv technique.
evidence: AC#4: 'No reference to a `per-extra`, `union`, or `import-linter` JOB remains in `docs/` or `.github/`, excluding `docs/experiments/**` archival corpora.'
Scope: 'Explicitly NOT in scope: the "three extras" count above; `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/*.jsonl`' — _optionality.yml is not listed as excluded.
_optionality.yml line 3-4: '# Reusable (workflow_call) form of the optionality contract — the clean-core-wheel,\n# per-extra, and union checks.'
_optionality.yml line 122: 'name: optional extras isolate (per-extra venvs + union)'
findings.finding: AC#4 ('No reference to a `per-extra`, `union`, or `import-linter` JOB remains in `docs/` or `.github/`') cannot be satisfied by the plan's two stated edits alone: `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` line 4 reads 'the clean-core-wheel, per-extra, and union checks' and line 122's job `name:` reads 'optional extras isolate (per-extra venvs + union)' — both are live occurrences of the forbidden strings in `.github/`. The scope excludes this file from edits, creating a direct contradiction between scope and AC.
scenarios: A reviewer running a grep for 'per-extra' in .github/ after the plan's two edits are applied will still find hits in _optionality.yml, causing AC#4 to fail.
A future maintainer auditing stale job references via AC#4's criterion will be confused by the surviving references in _optionality.yml.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow AC#4 to: 'No reference to a `per-extra`, `union`, or `import-linter` **job** (as a distinct CI job name) remains in `docs/` or `.github/` files outside `_optionality.yml` itself and `docs/experiments/**`.' — OR add _optionality.yml lines 3-4 and 122 to the edit scope with updated wording such as 'the clean-core-wheel and optional-extras checks' / 'optional extras isolate (per-extra venvs + union venv within one job)'.
